speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; can you tell me exactly how you are positioned right now and if you can move that leg at all?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Femoral Neck Fracture. Based on the mechanism of injury (rear-end collision), the patient's age (25), immediate onset of bilateral knee pain (indicating a femoral shaft or hip force transmission), and severe right groin pain combined with abnormal leg positioning, a femoral neck fracture is the primary concern requiring urgent orthopedic intervention to prevent avascular necrosis.
